findings.title: Salesforce refresh uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: The newly added token-refresh block calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma. Every Salesforce client construction that reaches the refresh block will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking Salesforce event creation, updates, searches, and deletions even when credential sharing is disabled.

findings.title: Google credential update stores the Zod SafeParse wrapper instead of the token
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result shaped {success, data}, but this code stores that whole object as the credential key. Previously the parsed credential itself was stored. After the first token refresh, credential.key no longer has access_token/refresh_token at the top level, so the next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) in googleAuth will fail and the Google Calendar credential becomes unusable. This affects normal non-sharing refreshes too.

findings.title: Minimum token schema strips real fields and fabricates a refresh_token
findings.body: When sharing is enabled, minimumTokenResponseSchema only declares access_token plus nonsense computed keys, and Zod strips undeclared fields such as expires_in, expiry timing, scope, token_type, and the real refresh_token. The helper then sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 and Zoom spread/copy that result into the stored credential, overwriting the real refresh token with a placeholder and losing expiry data (producing NaN expiry in Zoom), so the credential is corrupted and the next refresh fails.

findings.title: Sync path returns a fetch Response to callers expecting axios/SDK token objects
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response when sharing is enabled, but several wrapped refresh functions do not return fetch Responses: HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object with accessToken/expiresIn, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect an axios response with .data, and Google expects an object whose .data contains the token. In sharing mode those callers read undefined properties, compute NaN expiry dates, throw when dereferencing .data, or persist an empty/incorrect token object, so token refresh breaks for those apps instead of using the synced token.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential id as the Cal.com user id to the sync endpoint
findings.body: biginAuth/refreshAccessToken only receives credentialId (the Credential row id), and this call passes that value as refreshOAuthTokens' userId argument. The sync endpoint therefore receives calcomUserId=<credential id>, not the owner's user id, so it can return tokens for the wrong user or fail to find the user, causing wrong-account credentials or broken Zoho Bigin refreshes.

findings.title: Salesforce now refreshes unconditionally and then uses the old access token
findings.body: getClient now performs a Salesforce refresh-token POST on every service construction, regardless of whether the stored token is valid or credential sharing is configured, and rejects based on response.statusText !== "OK" even though statusText can be empty for successful HTTP/2 responses. Worse, after parsing/updating the refreshed token, the returned jsforce Connection is still built with credentialKey.access_token (the old token) at line 106, so the refresh cost/failure mode is added but the refreshed token is not used for the API connection.

findings.title: Lark refresh expects provider-shaped nested data that the sync contract does not provide
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens documents the sync endpoint response as only an access token and expiry date, but Lark's refresh code builds new credentials from data.data.refresh_token, data.data.refresh_expires_in, and data.data.expires_in. A minimal synced response will make those fields undefined, storing refresh_token=undefined and NaN refresh/access expiry dates in the credential and returning an undefined access token, corrupting the Lark credential after the first synced refresh.

findings.title: Webex synced refresh is rejected by the unchanged full Webex token schema
findings.body: When sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens is supposed to return only an access token and expiry, but Webex still validates the response with webexRefreshedTokenSchema, which requires the literal Webex scope, Bearer token_type, refresh_token, and refresh_token_expires_in. A minimal synced token response will always fail safeParse and reject with 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', so Webex cannot refresh tokens in sharing mode.

findings.title: Webhook handler lets validation and decryption errors throw as unhandled 500s
findings.body: The handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and later symmetricDecrypt plus JSON.parse with no try/catch or safeParse handling. Malformed JSON, an invalid userId/appSlug type, a bad encryption key, or non-JSON decrypted keys will throw out of the Next.js handler and produce an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 400 response, making integration failures hard to diagnose and retry correctly.

findings.title: Credential webhook has a find-then-create race that can create duplicates
findings.body: The handler does prisma.credential.findFirst for (userId, appId) and then creates a credential if none was found, with no unique constraint/upsert or transaction covering the check. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both create rows; later webhooks update only the findFirst row while other code may read a stale duplicate, leading to inconsistent synced credentials.

findings.title: No tests cover the credential-sharing webhook or refreshed-token branches
findings.body: This PR adds a security-sensitive webhook that authenticates with a shared secret, decrypts third-party OAuth keys, and creates/updates credentials, plus sharing branches in many token-refresh paths, but adds no tests for valid sync creation/update, wrong-secret rejection, disabled sharing, malformed encrypted payloads, or the sharing-enabled refresh behavior. The PR description also states tests were not added, so the credential-corruption and return-type regressions in these paths are not guarded against.
